articles.text:
Stord Secures $400 Million Credit Facility Led by Citi to Scale Its Network, Robotics, and AI Investment, Expands Leadership Team
News provided by
Stord
Oct 08, 2026, 09:30 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Oversubscribed at nearly double the company's original target and joined by Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and others. The financing arrives alongside two executive appointments: Bill Zerella as Chief Financial Officer and Mark Wayland as Chief Revenue Officer.
ATLANTA , Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stord , the physical intelligence layer for independent commerce, today announced a $400 million credit facility led by Citi and joined by Morgan Stanley and JPMorgan, alongside First Citizens, Citizens, and KeyBank. The company saw significant demand, closing the facility oversubscribed at nearly double the amount Stord originally went to market seeking.
The facility, combined with Stord's $250M Series F at a $3B valuation earlier in 2026, gives Stord substantial liquidity and financial flexibility as the company continues to grow, launch, and expand rapidly. This capital will fund Stord's rapid expansion of its fulfillment network, accelerate the automation and robotics work underway at Stord Labs, and deepen the commerce software and AI that brands rely on to grow revenue, reduce costs, and delight their consumers.
A key investment behind Stord's Series F and credit facility is Stord Labs, the company's physical intelligence lab at its Atlanta headquarters, which tests, develops, and deploys agentic robotics and AI across the Stord network on a single unified stack. That same team embeds forward deployed engineers directly inside Stord's own operations and its customers' businesses, and the results are already showing up in speed and accuracy across the network. With this new capital, Stord will further accelerate its investment in AI and automation across the network.
The financing is announced alongside two executive appointments. Bill Zerella joins as Chief Financial Officer. Zerella has led finance at three public companies, all of which he brought to the public equity markets, including Fitbit's IPO in 2015, where the company grew from roughly $300 million to more than $2 billion in revenue and reached a market capitalization of approximately $12 billion. He most recently served as Chief Financial Officer at ACV Auctions (NYSE: ACVA ), a $1 billion-plus business combining software, fintech , marketplace sales, and vehicle logistics. He understands brands the way Stord's customers do, and he has spent his career building finance inside complex, physical AI businesses like Stord's own.
Mark Wayland joins as Chief Revenue Officer. Wayland brings more than three decades of enterprise sales and revenue leadership, most recently as Chief Revenue Officer at Box (NYSE: BOX ). Before Box, he was Chief Revenue Officer at Tanium and spent more than a decade at Salesforce, rising to Senior Vice President of the Marketing Cloud. He has built global and enterprise sales organizations at public software companies throughout his career.
Stord is approaching $1 billion in revenue run-rate, has grown 10x over the past four years, and has secured $650 million in equity and credit capacity just in 2026 alone.

Reed Jobs’ Yosemite Raises $350 Million to Support Cancer Research
What if the next major breakthrough in cancer treatment is still sitting inside a university laboratory, waiting for the funding needed to move forward?
For Reed Jobs , the son of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs , the future of cancer care may depend on finding those discoveries early, supporting scientists willing to pursue unconventional ideas, and turning promising research into treatments that can reach patients.
Now, his cancer-focused venture capital firm, Yosemite, has closed its second fund at $350 million, marking a major step in its mission to make cancer a non-lethal disease within our lifetime.
The fundraising milestone was reported by Fortune on November 4, 2026, following an interview with Jobs in which he described the fund as oversubscribed, exceeding its original fundraising target.
The new capital brings together major pharmaceutical companies, research institutions, and technology investors around a model that combines traditional biotech venture capital with philanthropic funding for early-stage science.
Among Yosemite’s investors are Amgen , AbbVie , the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) , Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center , and venture capitalist John Doerr .
But the ambition behind the fund goes beyond investing in the next successful cancer drug. Yosemite wants to change how promising scientific discoveries are identified, financed, and ultimately translated into cancer treatments.
From a Personal Loss to a Mission Against Cancer
Reed Jobs’ interest in oncology began long before he entered venture capital.
His father, Steve Jobs, was diagnosed with a rare pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor and died in 2011. During his father’s illness, Reed began working in cancer research laboratories, an experience that helped shape his professional ambitions.
Rather than pursuing a career in technology, he focused on an equally complex challenge: reducing cancer mortality.
In 2023, Jobs founded Yosemite as an independent investment firm after spinning it out of Emerson Collective, the organization established by his mother, Laurene Powell Jobs .
Its central objective is deliberately different from the often-repeated ambition to cure cancer.
Jobs believes the more realistic long-term goal is to transform cancer from a frequently fatal disease into one that can increasingly be detected early, treated effectively, and managed over time.
Speaking during an October 28 episode of Fortune’s Term Sheet podcast, he summarized his motivation:
“The victory over death. That is what I want for cancer patients.”
Jobs has pointed to the transformation of HIV treatment as an example of how advances in medicine can dramatically reduce mortality from a once frequently fatal condition.
The analogy does not mean that all cancers can follow the same therapeutic pathway. Cancer encompasses hundreds of biologically distinct diseases, each presenting different challenges in detection, treatment, resistance, and recurrence.
Nevertheless, the goal highlights a growing emphasis in oncology on extending survival, preventing cancer-related deaths, and improving patients’ quality of life.
A $350 Million Fund With an Unusual Investment Strategy
Yosemite’s second fund represents a substantial expansion of its investment capacity.

Infinigence AI raises record 2.3b yuan in Series C funding round
By ZHENG YIRAN in Shanghai | chinadaily.com.cn
Updated: 2026-10-14 13:24
Share - WeChat
Xia Lixue, co-founder and CEO of Infinigence AI, delivers a speech during the World Artificial Intelligence Conference 2026 held in Shanghai in July. [Photo provided to chinadaily.com.cn]
Infinigence AI, a Chinese artificial intelligence-native infrastructure company, completed a 2.3 billion yuan ($343.7 million) Series C funding round on Monday, bringing its total funding since establishment to 4.3 billion yuan.
Both figures set records for single-round and cumulative fundraising in China's AI-native infrastructure sector, according to investment consulting firm ChinaVenture.
Founded in 2023 as a technology commercialization venture associated with Tsinghua University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Infinigence AI has attracted investors spanning state-backed funds, industrial investors and financial institutions. Its investors include Lenovo, Tencent, Baidu, HongShan Capital, Qiming Venture Partners and Shunwei Capital, alongside other investors.
The company focuses on connecting computing resources, AI model inference and industry applications through an infrastructure strategy it calls "Agentic Infra". Its framework comprises a computing resource hub, a token production platform and an AI productivity platform serving enterprise customers.
The company's computing platform has access to 37,000 petaflops of computing capacity and supports 16 types of mainstream chips, according to the company. It has also developed a heterogeneous computing platform designed to support large-scale model training across different chip architectures.
In July, Infinigence AI introduced a new inference architecture at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference. The company said the system reduced time to first token by 51.5 percent and could lower the cost per token by 37.5 percent.
Its agentic MaaS (model-as-a-service) platform recorded a 40-fold increase in daily token calls by July compared with December 2025, while the company said technical improvements had reduced inference costs by tenfold over the past year.

ASI has raised $325 million in a Series C funding round at a $3 billion valuation after securing federal contracts with a combined stated value of $974 million. The funding highlights investor interest in AI that forecasts and helps manage complex physical operations, including air traffic, power grids and military logistics.
ASI has raised $325 million in a Series C funding round that values the company at $3 billion . Spark Capital led the financing, with participation from affiliates of Citadel Securities, Meritech Capital, Craft Ventures, Energy Impact Partners and Andreessen Horowitz.
Formerly known as Air Space Intelligence, ASI develops simulation and monitoring software designed to help operators anticipate disruptions across complex systems, including air traffic, electricity networks and military operations. The company said it will use the new funding to expand deployments in energy, logistics and defence, while growing its research and engineering teams in Boston.
The funding follows two major US government awards in 2026: a 12-year, $875 million contract with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), announced in June, and a five-year Army contract with a maximum value of $99 million , awarded in September and announced publicly in October. These awards provide evidence of demand for ASI’s technology in aviation and military operations. However, their stated values represent multi-year contract amounts, not revenue already earned or guaranteed annual income.
The global Artificial Intelligence (AI) Software Market was valued at approximately $72.98 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $258.92 billion by 2035 , growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 13.5% from 2026 to 2035. Growing adoption of AI across industries is increasing demand for software that supports automation, predictive analysis and operational decision-making.
